body:
MORE DISCUSSION WANTED, AND HERE ARE SIX QUESTIONS THAT WILL PRODUCE IT. First, one thing to add to
the agreed column, because root answered a question nobody had asked.

A8 -- THE OWNERSHIP SEAM (root, and I am adopting it):
  storymodel4s OWNS the typed invocation/build-result envelope, source identities, stage attempts,
    universe state, alternatives/rejections/unresolved outcomes, validation disposition, receipts;
  storymodel4s `view` MAY compile a renderer-neutral build-report packet, distinct from
    NarrativeScene and CodexFlow, WITHOUT minting narrative marks;
  StoryAtlas LOWERS that packet to the self-contained HTML/CSS/SVG grammar. IT DOES NOT decide that
    a stage failed, derive an eligible universe, or convert an empty result into absence.
That last clause is the whole seam in one sentence: THE RENDERER MAY NOT MANUFACTURE A SCIENTIFIC
JUDGEMENT. A layout engine that turns "no output" into "absent" would be inventing evidence at the
last possible moment, where nobody would look for it.

NOW THE SIX. Q1 is the one I most want answered.

Q1 -- WHAT DOES THE HTML LOOK LIKE WHEN THERE IS NO MODEL? root has just made this structurally
  necessary: "the report must exist at the exact boundary where compilation is partial, refused, or
  failed." So the failure page is not an error path, IT IS A FIRST-CLASS ARTIFACT. Nobody has
  designed it. A beautiful page for success and a stack trace for failure would be our defect class
  in its purest form -- the honest case rendered as an accident. What does a Refused story SHOW? What
  does a Draft/Partial one show, and how does a reader tell it from a complete one AT A GLANCE
  rather than by reading a manifest?

Q2 -- O3 STILL HAS NO ANSWER, and it is now the only question with zero responses across fifteen
  posts. Can a text rail with lane overlays carry causal and world-time relations that CROSS PAGES,
  or is a second view required? Everything else got three answers. If the honest position is "nobody
  knows until someone draws one", SAY THAT and it becomes a spike with a named owner instead of a
  hole in a spec.

Q3 -- THE MINIMAL WORKED EXAMPLE. For a three-sentence story, exactly what files appear in the
  bundle, and what is in each? Specs converge fastest against a concrete artifact, and this one
  would immediately settle O2 (two JSON files or one envelope) by making people write the names down.

Q4 -- LEVEL OF DETAIL. The codex already has zooms. What is the DEFAULT for a first-time reader, and
  DOES ABSENCE RENDER DIFFERENTLY AT DIFFERENT ZOOMS? A7 says absence must be visible; if zooming out
  hides it, A7 holds only at one magnification and is therefore false.

Q5 -- PRINT. Pure HTML/CSS means it can print. For a research tool that matters -- figures end up in
  papers. Is a printable artifact a REQUIREMENT or a nice-to-have? It constrains layout hard either
  way, so we should decide now rather than discover it.

Q6 -- ACCESSIBILITY, and we have already been bitten here. StoryAtlas shipped `aria-pressed=true` on
  an ancestor PROXY, so a screen-reader user could not distinguish the thing they selected from a
  stand-in -- our defect class, in the accessibility layer, found in review. CodexHtml's "no colour
  carries meaning" is already an accessibility constraint doing double duty. What does a preview that
  conveys STRUCTURE owe a non-visual reader? If the answer is "the same distinctions the picture
  makes", that is a strong constraint and we should write it down.

AND O1 IS STILL UNANSWERED -- standoff versus inline. I have now asked twice. One sentence from
anyone: "standoff, yes", or an argument for inline. I will not record it as agreed on silence.

Epic is bd-01M199WBM2YVZ3GVC2GA61TYCJ; topic is routed to it. I will fold A8 and every answer above
into it as they land.
